_about: John Boyer's rulings on DK dash heads that rule E (2026-09-24) cannot settle from the print: {work: {column: ruling}}. `head` is the whole printed dash head, matched exactly (whitespace aside). A reading ruling carries `reading`: {author, work} as citation-dictionary.json keys plus the locus and any apparatus, or null while the ruling is pending (the head then stays verbatim, flagged by `pending`, default awaiting-adjudication). A correction (`type`: correction) fixes a DK misprint: `printed` is the misprint as the head prints it, `reading` the corrected citation, `readerNote` the note the reader shows after it (DRAFT copy until John approves it). `note` records the ruling and is never shown. The stage fails the build if a ruling's head is no longer in the text, or the citation above it names another author and work.

John, 2026-09-24: Clement's Stromateis keeps DK's own section numbers. The TLG's Stromateis numbers some of these sections one or two apart; the dash check (pipeline/tests/test_dash_citations_verified.py) accepts such a near miss in the same book, and nothing else.
